text: Why does Java use half-open ranges — include the start, exclude the end?
choices: Because it is faster to compute
Because C did it and Java copied C
Because arrays are indexed from zero
The count is the difference, adjacent ranges join without gaps, and empty is natural
explanation: A range from a to b half-open holds b − a elements with no adjustment; 0..k followed by k..n covers 0..n exactly once with no +1 at the join; and 0..0 is empty without writing an end below its start. Dijkstra set this out in EWD831 with the reasoning attached.
